Async task guide

Tasks schedule coroutine work and let an application coordinate several operations without blocking the whole process. A task owns one coroutine, records its result or exception, and exposes cancellation state to the caller. Applications normally create tasks through the running event loop and retain references for as long as the work matters. This chapter describes that contract in enough detail to use it safely.

Creating tasks

Create a task from a coroutine object, then await it directly or gather it with related work. Structured task groups provide a scope in which child failures cancel their siblings and are reported together. Naming important tasks makes diagnostics easier, while retaining the returned object prevents background work from disappearing before completion. These rules apply to each task described in this document.

Cancellation

Cancellation requests cooperative shutdown by arranging for a cancellation exception at the next suspension point. Cleanup code belongs in a finally block, and code that catches cancellation should normally propagate it after releasing resources. Timeouts use the same mechanism, so swallowing cancellation can violate surrounding task-group and timeout guarantees. The next documentation chapter covers streams, not a continuation of this page.
